metais help manifest — Every field of metais.yaml, inputs and outputs included.

Examples:

A complete metais.yaml: a package with two inputs, one of which may be supplied
as CSV, rendered to Markdown and to an HTML page that escapes its values.

  metais: "1.0"
  name: org.example.release-notes
  version: "1.2.0"
  title: Release notes
  description: Release notes for one product release, in Markdown and HTML.
  guide: |-
    Supply the release first, then its changes.

    Read inputs/changes.md for what a good change says.
  authors:
    - name: Example Docs Team
      email: docs@example.org
      url: https://example.org/docs
  license: Apache-2.0
  homepage: https://example.org/release-notes
  inputs:
    - name: release
      title: The release
      schema: inputs/release.schema.json
    - name: changes
      title: The changes in the release
      description: One change per row, newest first.
      schema: inputs/changes.schema.json
      meaning: inputs/changes.md
      forms: [json, yaml, csv]
      csv:
        delimiter: ";"
  outputs:
    - id: notes
      template: notes.md.liquid
    - id: page
      template: page.html.liquid
      path: "{{ inputs.release.version }}/index.html"
      escape: html

The same package's outputs could instead write one page per change with
for_each, and a zip holding a template, an asset and a mirror:

  outputs:
    - id: change_pages
      template: change.md.liquid
      for_each: inputs.changes
      when: item.public
      path: "changes/{{ item.id }}.md"
    - id: bundle
      path: "release-{{ inputs.release.version }}.zip"
      container:
        format: zip
        entries:
          - template: notes.md.liquid
            path: README.md
            first: true
          - asset: logo.png
            path: images/logo.png
            stored: true
          - mirror: site
            path: site
            escape: html

The manifest's top level:

  metais
      Required. The METAIS specification version the package targets, as a
      quoted string: unquoted, 1.0 is the number 1. A tool processes the package
      under exactly that version's rules.
      Example: metais: "1.0"
  name
      Required. The package's name: segments of lower-case ASCII letters and
      digits, single hyphens between them, joined by dots. A segment is at most
      63 characters and the name at most 128, and the first segment is not a
      Windows device name (con, prn, aux, nul, com0 to com9, lpt0 to lpt9). A
      package published beyond its author should begin with a domain its
      publisher controls, reversed.
      Example: name: org.example.release-notes
  version
      Required. The package's own version, a Semantic Versioning 2.0.0 version
      of at most 128 characters, without a leading v and quoted. Pre-release and
      build metadata are allowed.
      Example: version: "1.2.0-rc.1"
  title
      Required. What the package is, as a person names it: one line of 1 to 200
      characters.
      Example: title: Release notes
  description
      Required. What the package produces, in a sentence or a short paragraph of
      1 to 1000 characters, displayed verbatim.
      Example: description: Release notes for one product release.
  guide
      Required. The guide for suppliers, in CommonMark, of 1 to 16384
      characters: what the package is for, how its inputs relate, the order to
      gather them in, and where to read further. It may not end with a line
      break, so write a block as guide: |- rather than guide: |.
      Example: guide: Supply the release first, then its changes.
  authors
      Optional. The package's authors, 1 to 64 people or organizations, each an
      object with the fields under authors[].
      Example: authors: [{name: Example Docs Team}]
  license
      Optional. The terms of the package's own content, an SPDX license
      expression of 1 to 512 characters with AND, OR and WITH in upper case.
      Identifiers are not checked against the SPDX License List.
      Example: license: Apache-2.0 OR MIT
  homepage
      Optional. The package's home page, an absolute https or http URI of at
      most 2048 characters, with a host, no user information and no fragment. No
      command ever fetches it.
      Example: homepage: https://example.org/release-notes
  inputs
      Required. The inputs the package takes, in the order a supplier meets
      them, each an object with the fields under inputs[]. It may be empty.
      Example: inputs: []
  input_constraints
      Optional. The package path, under inputs/ and ending .json, .yaml or .yml,
      of a schema evaluated against the object holding every input, for rules
      that relate one input to another.
      Example: input_constraints: inputs/constraints.schema.json
  outputs
      Required. The output declarations, at least one, in the order they are
      planned, each with the fields under outputs[].
      Example: outputs: [{id: notes, template: notes.md.liquid}]

Each author, authors[]:

  authors[].name
      Required. The person or organization: one line of 1 to 200 characters.
      Example: name: Ada Lovelace
  authors[].email
      Optional. An email address of 3 to 254 characters, with exactly one @ and
      no space. It is not validated further, and no command sends mail.
      Example: email: ada@example.org
  authors[].url
      Optional. The author's web page, an absolute https or http URI with a host
      and no user information, as homepage.
      Example: url: https://example.org/ada

Each input, inputs[] (spec chapter 5):

  inputs[].name
      Required. The input's name, unique among the inputs: a lower-case letter,
      then up to 63 lower-case letters, digits and underscores, and none of
      Liquid's reserved words blank, empty, false, first, last, nil, null, size
      and true. A template reads the input as inputs.<name>, a data directory's
      file for it is named after it, and it is the first token of a --set
      pointer.
      Example: name: changes
  inputs[].title
      Required. What the input is, in brief: one line of 1 to 200 characters.
      Example: title: The changes in the release
  inputs[].description
      Optional. What the input means, as plain text, line breaks allowed.
      Example: description: One change per row, newest first.
  inputs[].schema
      Required. The package path, under inputs/, of the input's JSON Schema
      file, ending .json, .yaml or .yml.
      Example: schema: inputs/changes.schema.json
  inputs[].meaning
      Optional. The package path, under inputs/, of a CommonMark document ending
      .md that says what the data is for and what good data looks like. No tool
      interprets it.
      Example: meaning: inputs/changes.md
  inputs[].forms
      Optional. The file forms the input may be supplied in, each at most once,
      of json, yaml, csv, text and markdown. Default: json and yaml.
      Example: forms: [json, yaml, csv]
  inputs[].csv
      Optional, and allowed only when forms holds csv. How a CSV file of the
      input is read: an object whose one member is delimiter.
      Example: csv: {delimiter: ";"}
  inputs[].csv.delimiter
      Required in csv. The character that separates fields: a comma, a
      semicolon, a vertical bar or a tab.
      Example: delimiter: "\t"
  inputs[].collection
      Optional. true for a collection: an array of items, supplied as a
      directory of item files. Default false.
      Example: collection: true
  inputs[].required
      Optional. false for an input a supplier may leave out. Default true.
      Example: required: false

Each output declaration, outputs[] (spec chapters 9 and 10):
A declaration takes exactly one form, named by the one source key it carries:
template, asset, mirror or container. Each field below names the forms that take
it, and a form refuses any other field.

  outputs[].id
      Every form. Required at the top level and optional on a container entry.
      The declaration's identifier: a lower-case letter, then up to 63
      lower-case letters, digits and underscores, unique among the top-level
      declarations, and an entry's among its container's entries.
      Example: id: change_pages
  outputs[].template
      The template form's source key: the template's path relative to
      templates/, rendered to one file per evaluation.
      Example: template: notes.md.liquid
  outputs[].asset
      The asset form's source key: a file or a directory relative to assets/, .
      being the whole of assets/. Every file is copied byte for byte, never
      rendered.
      Example: asset: images
  outputs[].mirror
      The mirror form's source key: a directory relative to templates/, . being
      the whole of templates/, whose every template is rendered to its relative
      path with a final .liquid removed. A template whose name, or a directory's
      between it and the mirror's, begins with _ is a partial and is not
      mirrored, and nor is a template a template field names.
      Example: mirror: site
  outputs[].container
      The container form's source key: the zip's shape, an object with the
      fields under outputs[].container.
      Example: container: {entries: [{template: notes.md.liquid}]}
  outputs[].path
      Every form. Required on a container and with for_each, and optional
      otherwise. The destination relative to the root of the tree, a Liquid
      template that is never escaped; for an asset directory or a mirror it
      names a directory, . being the root. Without it, a template output is
      written to its template's path with a final .liquid removed, an asset to
      its path under assets/, and a mirror beneath its directory. Quote a path
      that begins with {.
      Example: path: "changes/{{ item.id }}.md"
  outputs[].when
      Every form. Optional. A Liquid condition, what may follow if in {% if %}:
      the declaration writes files only where it holds, and without when it
      always holds. With for_each it is judged once per element.
      Example: when: inputs.release.public
  outputs[].for_each
      Template and container forms. Optional, and needs path. A Liquid value
      expression, what may appear inside {{ }}: its array gives one evaluation
      per element, in order, with the element bound to item and its position to
      fan_out, and nil gives none. A declaration beneath a container with
      for_each has none of its own.
      Example: for_each: inputs.changes
  outputs[].escape
      Template and mirror forms. Optional. How the values a template writes are
      escaped: none, the default, or html, which writes & < > " and ' as
      entities.
      Example: escape: html
  outputs[].newline
      Template and mirror forms. Optional. The rendered file's line endings:
      as-written, the default, or crlf, which makes every LF not preceded by CR
      a CR LF before the file is validated.
      Example: newline: crlf
  outputs[].validate
      Template form. Optional. The package path, outside .compiled/, of a JSON
      Schema the file's final bytes are validated against, parsed by its kind,
      which must be json or yaml. A file that fails refuses the render, and
      nothing is written.
      Example: validate: schemas/feed.schema.json
  outputs[].kind
      Template form. Optional. The output kind of every file it renders,
      overriding the one its path's extension gives: html, xml, markdown, json,
      yaml, csv, css, hash, slash, sql or text. The kind chooses the comment
      syntax provenance writes; it is not escaping.
      Example: kind: yaml
  outputs[].executable
      Template and asset forms, never a container entry. Optional. true writes
      the file with mode 0755 instead of 0644, less the umask. Default false.
      Example: executable: true

A zip container's shape, outputs[].container (spec chapter 10):

  outputs[].container.format
      Optional. The container's format: zip is the only one.
      Example: format: zip
  outputs[].container.profile
      Optional. The packaging rules of a format the container follows: ooxml,
      which needs an entry [Content_Types].xml; odf, which writes the mimetype
      entry first and needs META-INF/manifest.xml; or epub, which writes the
      mimetype entry first and needs META-INF/container.xml. Without one, the
      container is written exactly as declared.
      Example: profile: epub
  outputs[].container.mimetype
      Required with the odf profile, and allowed only with it. The media type,
      type/subtype, written as the mimetype entry.
      Example: mimetype: application/vnd.oasis.opendocument.text
  outputs[].container.entries
      Required. The container's entries, at least one, each a declaration with
      the fields under outputs[].container.entries[].
      Example: entries: [{template: notes.md.liquid, path: README.md}]

Each container entry, outputs[].container.entries[]:
An entry is a declaration of one of the four forms and takes the fields
outputs[] gives its form, except that id is optional, executable is refused,
since a zip records no file mode, and path names the entry inside the container.
Entries are written into the container only; a part that must also be a file of
its own is declared again at the top level. Two fields are an entry's alone:

  outputs[].container.entries[].first
      Optional. true places the entry's files before every other entry the
      profile does not place, in declaration order. Default false.
      Example: first: true
  outputs[].container.entries[].stored
      Optional. true stores the entry's files rather than compressing them.
      Default false.
      Example: stored: true

metais check [<dir>] checks a package's manifest against these rules, with every
other step, and reports every finding at once; a package that cannot be read at
all gets only the findings of that refusal. metais init writes a package to
start from. metais help templates covers the template language a template, path,
when and for_each are written in. The specification's chapter 3 (the manifest),
chapter 5 (inputs), chapter 9 (outputs) and chapter 10 (containers and
transforms) state each rule, and schemas/1.0/manifest.schema.json holds the
manifest's schema.
